source_text: Καὶ ἱερουργήσω σοι τὴν τῆς αἰνέσεως θυσίαν, μυρίων ὁλοκαυτωμάτων προτιμοτέραν σοὶ τῷ ἀπροσδεεῖ καὶ τελείῳ Θεῷ, ὃς οὐκ ἀπαιτεῖς σωματικὰς θυσίας, ἐν αἷς πλεονεκτοῦσιν οἱ εὐπορώτεροι, ἀλλὰ τὴν ἀπὸ διαθέσεως καὶ καρδίας ἀληθινῆς ἐξομολόγησιν, ἧς μέτεστι πᾶσιν ἐξ ἴσου τοῖς βουλομένοις. Τὰς εὐχάς μου τῷ Κυρίῳ ἀποδώσω ἐναντίον παντὸς τοῦ λαοῦ αὐτοῦ. Θύων δέ σοι τὴν αἴνεσιν, οὐχ ὡς ἐπαισχυνόμενος, λάθρα που καὶ ἐν παραβύστῳ θύσω, φεύγων τὰς μέμψεις τῶν ἀσεβῶν· ἀλλὰ πάνδημόν τινα θυσίαν ἐπιτελέσω, τὸν λαὸν ὅλον κοινωνὸν τῆς λατρείας παραλαβών. Τόπος δὲ ἡμῖν τῆς θυσίας ἀποδειχθήσεται τὰ μέσα καὶ περιφανέστατα τῆς Ἱερουσαλήμ. Ἀκούσατε, οἱ τὴν Ἐκκλησίαν καταλιμπάνοντες, καὶ ἐν οἴκοις κοινοῖς συστρεφόμενοι, τὰ ἄθλια τοῦ τιμίου σώματος ἀποῤῥήγματα, ὅτι χρὴ τὰς εὐχὰς ἀποδιδόναι ἐν μέσῳ τῆς Ἱερουσαλήμ· τουτέστι, τῆς Ἐκκλησίας τοῦ Θεοῦ. Οὐδὲ γὰρ κατὰ τὴν παλαιὰν λατρείαν ἴδιον ἐξῆν ἑκάστῳ πήγνυσθαι θυσιαστήριον, ἀλλ' ἓν ἀποδέδεικτο τοῖς θυσιάζειν προαιρουμένοις. Σὺ δὲ ἀντεγείρεις τῷ τῶν πατέρων θυσιαστηρίῳ βωμὸν, καὶ πῦρ ἀνάπτεις ἀλλότριον ἐπ' αὐτοῦ, μηδὲ τῷ παλαιῷ παραδείγματι σωφρονιζόμενος, ἀνθρώπους κατεφθαρμένους τὸν νοῦν ἐπισπώμενος, καὶ συμμιαίνων αὐτοῖς ἑαυτόν. Ὧν φύγοιτε τὴν μίμησιν, ὑμεῖς ὁ λαὸς τοῦ Κυρίου, καὶ μὴ χωρισθείητε τῆς μερίδος τῶν σωζομένων, διαμένοντες ἐν τῇ πίστει, τελειούμενοι ἐν ταῖς ἐντολαῖς τοῦ Κυρίου, ᾧ ἡ δόξα καὶ τὸ κράτος, εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν.
thought_title: The public sacrifice of praise in the Church
orientation: Basil is closing the homily by explaining the psalmist's vow to offer the sacrifice of praise publicly in Jerusalem, which he identifies with the Church of God, and he warns those who leave the Church for private gatherings.
pass_a_gloss: And I will offer to you the sacrifice of praise, more honorable to you than ten thousand whole burnt offerings, to you the needless and perfect God, who do not demand bodily sacrifices, in which the wealthier have the advantage, but the confession from disposition and true heart, which is available to all equally who wish it. I will pay my vows to the Lord before all his people. And sacrificing to you the praise, not as one ashamed, I will not sacrifice secretly somewhere and in a hidden corner, fleeing the reproaches of the impious; but I will perform a public sacrifice, taking the whole people as partner of the worship. And the place of the sacrifice for us will be shown to be the middle and most conspicuous parts of Jerusalem. Hear, you who abandon the Church and gather in common houses, the wretched fragments torn from the honored body, that it is necessary to pay the vows in the middle of Jerusalem; that is, of the Church of God. For not even according to the old worship was it permitted for each person to set up a private altar, but one was shown to those choosing to sacrifice. But you raise up against the altar of the fathers a shrine, and you kindle alien fire upon it, not even being chastened by the old example, drawing to yourself men corrupted in mind, and defiling yourself together with them. May you flee the imitation of these, you the people of the Lord, and may you not be separated from the portion of those being saved, remaining in the faith, being perfected in the commandments of the Lord, to whom be the glory and the might, to the ages of ages. Amen.

lemmas.gloss: I will offer as a sacred rite

choices.term: ἱερουργήσω σοι τὴν τῆς αἰνέσεως θυσίαν
choices.english: I will offer to you the sacrifice of praise
choices.why: Keeps the verb's sacred-rite force and the fixed glossary rendering 'sacrifice of praise' for θυσία αἰνέσεως.
rejected: I will sacrifice to you the praise offering
I will perform for you the thanksgiving sacrifice

choices.english: more honorable to you than ten thousand whole burnt offerings
choices.why: μυρίων is a round number for a vast multitude; 'whole burnt offerings' preserves the LXX technical term for ὁλοκαύτωμα.
rejected: more valued than myriads of holocausts

choices.english: to you the needless and perfect God
choices.why: ἀπροσδεής means lacking nothing, needing no gift; 'needless' is concise and literal.
rejected: the God who needs nothing and is perfect

choices.why: παράβυστος denotes a secret, out-of-the-way place; 'hidden corner' captures the spatial secrecy.

choices.term: τὰ ἄθλια τοῦ τιμίου σώματος ἀποῤῥήγματα
choices.english: the wretched fragments torn from the honored body
choices.why: ἀποῤῥήγματα are pieces violently broken off; the phrase describes schismatics as torn from the Church's body.
rejected: the miserable splinters of the precious body
the pitiful shreds of the honored body

choices.why: βωμός is a pagan altar or shrine, deliberately contrasted with θυσιαστήριον; 'shrine' marks the non-biblical, idolatrous character.

pass_b_english: And I will offer to you the sacrifice of praise, more honorable to you than ten thousand whole burnt offerings—to you, the self-sufficient and perfect God, who do not demand bodily sacrifices, in which the wealthy have the advantage, but rather the confession that comes from a sincere disposition and heart, which is equally available to all who desire it. “I will pay my vows to the Lord in the presence of all his people” (Psalm 115:8 LXX; Psalm 116:14 Hebrew). When I offer you praise, I will not do it secretly, in some hidden corner, as if ashamed and fleeing the reproaches of the ungodly. No, I will perform a public sacrifice, taking the whole people as partners in the worship. And the place appointed for our sacrifice will be the very center and most conspicuous parts of Jerusalem.

Listen, you who abandon the Church and gather in ordinary houses, you wretched fragments torn from the precious body: vows must be paid in the midst of Jerusalem—that is, in the Church of God. For even under the old worship, no one was permitted to set up a private altar; one altar alone was appointed for those who chose to sacrifice. But you raise up an altar against the altar of the fathers, and you kindle alien fire upon it, not even being corrected by the ancient example. You draw in people whose minds are corrupted, and you defile yourself along with them. May you flee from imitating those people, you people of the Lord, and do not be separated from the portion of those who are being saved. Remain in the faith, being perfected in the commandments of the Lord, to whom be glory and power forever and ever. Amen.

problems.quote: wretched fragments torn from the honored body
problems.source_quote: τὰ ἄθλια τοῦ τιμίου σώματος ἀποῤῥήγματα
problems.why: 'Honored body' is wrong; τὸ τίμιον σῶμα is the precious/honorable body (the Church), but 'wretched fragments' misrepresents ἄθλια as 'wretched' rather than 'wretched/pitiful torn-off pieces'.
problems.fix: you pitiful fragments torn from the precious body

problems.why: 'Shrine' is too general; βωμός specifically means altar, creating direct contrast with θυσιαστήριον.

edits.new: you pitiful fragments torn from the precious body

edits.old: you raise up a shrine against the altar of the fathers
edits.new: you raise up an altar against the altar of the fathers

fixed: Changed 'wretched fragments torn from the honored body' to 'pitiful fragments torn from the precious body' because ἄθλια means pitiful/wretched and τίμιον means precious/honorable, not 'honored'.
Changed 'shrine' to 'altar' because βωμός specifically means altar, creating a direct contrast with θυσιαστήριον.

problems.why: The optative φύγοιτε expresses a wish/prayer ('may you flee'), but the English 'Flee from imitating them' is an imperative, losing the optative's hortatory/desiderative force and the 'may you' prayer form.
problems.fix: May you flee from imitating them
problems.ruling: Optative φύγοιτε expresses wish 'may you flee'; imperative 'Flee' changes mood and force.

edits.new: May you flee from imitating them

fixed: The optative φύγοιτε expresses a wish/prayer, so 'May you flee from imitating them' is correct; the English imperative lost that force.

problems.quote: you pitiful fragments torn from the precious body
problems.source_quote: τὰ ἄθλια τοῦ τιμίου σώματος ἀποῤῥήγματα
problems.why: The Greek is a vocative address to the people described as 'wretched fragments'; English makes it an apostrophe to 'you' as fragments, but 'pitiful' weakens ἄθλια ('wretched, miserable') and the syntax is awkward.
problems.fix: you wretched fragments torn from the precious body

problems.quote: May you flee from imitating them
problems.why: Ὧν is genitive plural masculine, referring to the people just described (ἀνθρώπους κατεφθαρμένους), not 'them' as a separate group; 'flee their imitation' means 'flee from imitating those people'.
problems.fix: May you flee from imitating those people

problems.why: 'Needless' means 'not needed'; ἀπροσδεής means 'needing nothing, self-sufficient', a divine attribute.
problems.ruling: ἀπροσδεεῖ means 'needing nothing/self-sufficient'; 'needless' means 'unnecessary,' reversing the sense.

fixed: Changed 'them' to 'those people' to clarify the referent of Ὧν.

last_rejected.why: Greek says 'more precious than ten thousand whole burnt offerings,' not 'more honorable to you.'
last_rejected.fix: more precious than ten thousand whole burnt offerings—to you
last_rejected.ruling: προτιμοτέραν σοί = 'more precious/honorable to you'; 'honorable' is within normal range of προτιμέω.

last_rejected.why: ἀπροσδεής means 'needing nothing,' not 'self-sufficient' which implies active sufficiency rather than lack of need.
last_rejected.ruling: ἀπροσδεής = 'needing nothing'; 'self-sufficient' is a standard equivalent, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.why: ἀληθινῆς modifies the confession, not disposition; 'true confession from disposition and heart.'
last_rejected.fix: the confession from disposition and true heart
last_rejected.ruling: ἀληθινῆς can modify either noun; 'sincere disposition and heart' is a valid reading, not a clear error.

last_rejected.why: κοινοῖς means 'common' in sense of shared/public, not 'ordinary'; these are house-church gatherings, not mundane homes.
last_rejected.ruling: κοινοῖς = 'common/shared'; 'ordinary' is within range; no meaning lost for readers.
